advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass `["CURRENT_REVISION"]` to `client.get_change(wip.change_id)` in handle_rebase_conflict so tip_sha is populated against real Gerrit.
evidence: infra/autolander/failure.py:169: `tip_sha = client.get_change(wip.change_id).get("current_revision")`
infra/autolander/failure.py:84: `current = client.get_change(change_id, ["CURRENT_REVISION"]).get("current_revision")` — the read-side correctly passes the opt
loop.py:180: `change = client.get_change(member_id, ["CURRENT_REVISION"])` — codebase convention: current_revision requires the opt
loop.py:74: `fetched = client.get_change(change_id, ["CURRENT_REVISION", "CURRENT_COMMIT"])`
ABSENCE: masked in tests because RecordingClient.get_change (tests/autolander/_autolander_fakes.py:84-89) returns current_revision irrespective of opts
advisory.finding: handle_rebase_conflict reads the tip SHA via `client.get_change(wip.change_id)` WITHOUT the `CURRENT_REVISION` option, so against real Gerrit `current_revision` is absent and `tip_sha` is None; the persisted marker's `patchset_sha` becomes None and never matches `get_valid` (which passes the opt), breaking self-invalidation.
scenarios: A real 409 rebase-conflict: marker written with patchset_sha=None; every subsequent get_valid returns None so restart re-drive and self-invalidation never work as intended

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a per-transition debug log line (record / label-removal / acknowledge / recheck) as the ticket AC requires.
evidence: ticket 0525-6d71-8969-4512 AC: 'Keep a rolling per-transition log line for debugging.' (repeated in Outcome record + AC)
ABSENCE: no `logging` import or log call anywhere in infra/autolander/failure.py (module read in full, lines 1-198)
advisory.finding: The ticket AC requires 'a rolling per-transition log line for debugging' (stated twice), but failure.py emits no logging at all — no `import logging`, no log calls on record/removal/acknowledge/recheck transitions.
scenarios: Operators debugging a stuck/handed-back stack have no per-transition trail since the marker store is single-slot

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether rebase-conflict hand-back should post an explanatory comment (as loop.py hand_back does) and correct/align loop.py's hand_back docstring accordingly.
evidence: infra/autolander/failure.py:118: `client.set_review(member_id, labels={"Autosubmit": 0})` — no message
loop.py:200-202: hand_back posts `message=comment` (HANDBACK_COMMENT) alongside removing Autosubmit
loop.py:199 docstring: 'Same hand-back mechanism S3 uses for conflict/CI-fail.'
ticket AC: CI-fail explicitly says 'post NO bot comment' but the rebase-conflict AC has no such no-comment instruction
advisory.finding: The rebase-conflict hand-back (remove_autosubmit_from_stack) posts NO Gerrit comment, unlike loop.py's existing hand_back which posts HANDBACK_COMMENT; a rebase conflict leaves no on-change signal for the owning agent (the needs_rebase marker is project-infra state, not visible on Gerrit), and hand_back's docstring claim that it is the 'Same hand-back mechanism S3 uses for conflict/CI-fail' is now inaccurate.
scenarios: An agent whose stack is handed back for a rebase conflict sees Autosubmit silently removed with no explanation on the change

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the recheck bound must survive restart; if so, derive rechecking from Gerrit (existing recheck comment / Verified state) rather than in-memory flag.
evidence: infra/autolander/failure.py:137-139: `if not wip.rechecking: client.set_review(wip.change_id, message=RECHECK_COMMENT); wip.rechecking = True`
loop.py:170-171: `rechecking: bool = False  # S3-owned in-flight sub-state ... NOT a new S2 phase` — only in the in-memory dataclass, not persisted
ABSENCE: no persistence of rechecking state; only needs_rebase markers are persisted (module docstring lines 8-9)
advisory.finding: `wip.rechecking` is in-memory WipChain state (never persisted), so after a restart while a bounded auto-recheck is pending, auto_recheck will re-post the `recheck` comment, violating the documented 'ONE recheck per patchset' bound.
scenarios: Auto-lander restarts after posting recheck but before the terminal vote; on re-entry rechecking is False again and recheck is posted a second time

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that calls auto_recheck with wip.rechecking already True (or twice) and asserts the `recheck` comment is posted at most ONCE.
evidence: failure.py:137-139 `if not wip.rechecking:` / `client.set_review(wip.change_id, message=RECHECK_COMMENT)` / `wip.rechecking = True`
test asserts `len(rechecks) == 1` but only after a single fresh-flag invocation: `auto_recheck(client, wip, await_terminal_verified=lambda cl, w: 1)`
ABSENCE: no test invokes auto_recheck with `wip.rechecking=True` (or invokes it twice) to prove no second `recheck` comment is posted — the guard the diff adds is regression-blind
advisory.finding: auto_recheck's re-post guard (the `if not wip.rechecking` bound-to-ONE-recheck behavior, the stated purpose of the new `rechecking` flag) is not tested; the single existing test starts with `rechecking=False` and a single invocation posts at most once regardless of the guard, so deleting the guard would not fail any test.
scenarios: A regression removes/inverts the `if not wip.rechecking` guard and re-posts `recheck` on every drive loop, spamming Gerrit — no test catches it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a case that pre-sets `wip.rechecking=True`, calls auto_recheck, and asserts zero new `recheck` messages were posted.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests that a 409 GerritError is treated as a no-op and a non-404/409 (e.g. 500) is re-raised by remove_autosubmit_from_stack.
evidence: failure.py:119-122 `except GerritError as exc:` / `if getattr(exc, 'status', None) in (404, 409): continue` / `raise`
only test uses `set_review_errors={"Ia": GerritError(404, "not found")}` — 404 only
ABSENCE: no test asserts a 409 is swallowed, and none asserts a non-404/409 (e.g. 500) is re-raised
advisory.finding: remove_autosubmit_from_stack's 409 no-op branch and its re-raise branch for non-404/409 GerritError statuses are untested; only the 404 no-op is exercised.
scenarios: A regression narrows the no-op set to just 404 (dropping 409) or broadens it to swallow all errors — neither is caught.
A genuine failure (500) that should abort/propagate is silently swallowed.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add two cases: one with a 409 error asserting no raise + both members attempted, one with a 500 error asserting the GerritError propagates.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test where remove_autosubmit_from_stack raises (non-idempotent status) and assert handle_rebase_conflict has already persisted an unacknowledged needs_rebase marker.
evidence: failure.py:180-182 `store.upsert(marker)  # record BEFORE removal` / `remove_autosubmit_from_stack(client, wip)` / `store.acknowledge(...)`
happy-path test only exercises successful removal where the marker ends `acknowledged is True`
ABSENCE: no test forces removal to raise (non-404/409) and asserts the marker is already persisted with `acknowledged=False` so restart re-drive can complete it
advisory.finding: The 'record marker BEFORE label removal' idempotent-ordering invariant is not verified against a failing removal; the marker's persistence when removal cannot complete (unacknowledged, later re-driven) is untested.
scenarios: A regression reorders upsert after removal; if removal raises the marker is lost and the stack is stuck with Autosubmit but no re-drive marker — undetected.
